record.paper_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can physical-layer security schemes be developed to secure uplink satellite communication from terrestrial or aerial devices to satellites, when the uplink is vulnerable to spoofing, message alteration, and denial-of-service attacks, carries large volumes of user data in broadband satellite systems, and must operate under performance and power constraints across heterogeneous devices and scenarios?

evidence.quote: However, uplink communication from any terrestrial or aerial device to the satellite is vulnerable to several attacks such as spoofing and alteration by malicious adversaries. Especially in broadband satellite communication, the uplink handles a huge amount of data sent by users to the satellite, and this data must be secured through schemes suitable for heterogeneous devices and scenarios.
Hence, researchers should give more attention to securing uplink communication using PLS, considering performance and power constraints.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a satellite communication system whose uplink channel carries data from a heterogeneous population of terrestrial and aerial transmitters (e.g., handheld terminals, IoT sensors, UAVs, ground gateways) to one or more satellites in low, medium, or geostationary orbit. Each transmitter i has a finite transmit-power budget P_i, a hardware/computational complexity bound C_i, and a minimum throughput requirement R_i. The uplink is subject to (i) eavesdropping by passive adversaries, (ii) spoofing in which an adversary impersonates a legitimate transmitter, (iii) message alteration in which an adversary modifies a transmitted codeword, and (iv) denial-of-service attacks (jamming) that inject interference into the uplink band. Channel state information about the legitimate user-to-satellite link may be partial, while channel information about the adversaries is unknown beyond statistical models.

Within the framework of physical-layer security (which uses channel coding, beamforming/precoding, artificial-noise injection, cooperative jamming, secret-key generation from channel reciprocity, and authentication based on physical channel features rather than upper-layer cryptography), formulate and design a scheme that simultaneously:

1. Achieves a positive secrecy rate R_s(i) ≥ R_i^{sec} for each legitimate transmitter i against the eavesdropping model, subject to P_i and C_i.
2. Provides a physical-layer authentication test, based on measurable channel features, whose false-acceptance probability against spoofing and message-alteration attacks is at most ε_FA and whose false-rejection probability for legitimate users is at most ε_FR.
3. Maintains a guaranteed availability (probability of successful decoding) of at least 1 − δ under a specified jamming model with adversary power budget P_J.
4. Operates uniformly across the heterogeneity of devices and orbital scenarios (LEO/MEO/GEO with their associated Doppler, latency, and path-loss regimes).

Characterize the fundamental trade-off region among the tuples (R_s, ε_FA, ε_FR, δ, P_i, P_J) achievable by any such scheme, and exhibit an explicit construction (coding, precoding, and authentication procedure) that attains a point inside this region under realistic satellite channel models (Rician/shadowed-Rician fading, large Doppler shifts, long propagation delays).
artifact.status_search_result: Securing satellite uplinks via physical-layer security is widely identified as an open research direction in recent surveys on satellite PLS; no general construction simultaneously addressing secrecy, authentication, and anti-jamming under heterogeneous device/power constraints is established in the literature, and only partial results exist for individual sub-problems (e.g., secrecy capacity bounds for shadowed-Rician channels, channel-based authentication prototypes).

status_evidence.title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Researchers should give more attention to securing uplink communication using PLS, considering performance and power constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Uplink PLS for satellite communication is identified as an open problem requiring further research.
